Definition: Whether government taxes, customs duties, and other revenue can be paid using the instant digital payment system, indicating integration of payment infrastructure with tax administration systems.
Comments: RRA supports revenue collection via digital payment channels (RRA 'Digital payment' guidance lists mobile money, mobile banking, internet banking as available digital payment systems for RRA payments).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed via current RRA service pages: income tax, VAT, withholding tax and excise duty can all be paid via e-Payment (internet/bank), mobile money (MTN/Airtel) or bank deposit, corroborating comprehensive digital revenue collection. The original single PDF source was inaccessible (403) but the claim is independently confirmed on live RRA pages; score unchanged at 3 (Yes).

Definition: Whether the instant payment system enables or plans to enable instant payments across national borders to other countries or regional payment systems, supporting remittances, trade, and regional integration.
Comments: Cross-border capability is under development/partially functional: EAC began implementing a regional instant payment pilot linking Tanzania’s TIPS with Rwanda’s National Payment Switch (RSwitch) to enable real-time cross-border transfers.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Corroborated with KT Press (Nov 2025) and a follow-up report dated February 2026: the Rwanda-Tanzania TIPS-RSwitch linkage remains a proof-of-concept pilot in technical and regulatory build-out, with no evidence of live, user-facing cross-border transactions as of early 2026. This matches 'Under development' rather than 'Partially functional', which implies some operational service already exists; revised down from 4 to 3.

Definition: Whether the system enables citizen payments to government for taxes, fees, licenses, fines, utility bills, and other government service charges.
Comments: Rwanda supports person-to-government digital payments via Rwanda Revenue Authority (RRA) ‘Digital payment’ guidance noting access to Mobile Money, Mobile Banking, Internet Banking etc. for paying taxes/fees.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Strongly corroborated beyond taxes: IremboGov, Rwanda's government services portal, confirms digital payment of licences, permits and traffic fines via mobile money, bank cards and bank transfer, in addition to RRA's tax payment channels. Score unchanged at 3 (Yes - Active Use).

Definition: Whether consumer protection legislation or regulations specifically address digital payment services, covering disclosure requirements, liability allocation for unauthorized transactions, error resolution procedures, and user rights.
Comments: The payment-system law includes consumer protection requirements: Art. 28 requires payment service providers to protect consumers of payment services in accordance with relevant laws/regulations; and includes dispute settlement provisions for disputes between operators/participants (e.g., Art. 52).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed via the Law Governing the Payment System (Law 61/2021, Arts 28 and 52) and independently via AfricaNenda's 2023 SIIPS Rwanda case study, which notes a dedicated Financial Service Consumer Protection Act (2021) and that eKash scheme rules embed liability demarcation and SLA-based dispute resolution. Score unchanged at 3 (Yes).

Score unchanged at 3 (Yes - Fully Public), now resting on a stronger, independent source.
